old: 1. Draw one invader token at random and keep it face down: a standard invader token if the mini-boss has not been defeated, an advanced invader token if it has.
new: 1. Draw one invader token at random and keep it face down: a standard invader token if the mini-boss has not been defeated, an advanced invader token if it has. In campaign play, draw a standard invader token while the current tier is tier one and an advanced invader token once it is tier two (see §18.1, Section Setup).
rationale: The numbered step gave only the standard-game test; §12.2's opening paragraph and §18.1 key the token to the current tier in campaign play.

old: Some campaigns place named invaders in listed encounters and use no invader tokens (see §19.3; §19.4).
new: Some campaigns place named invaders in listed encounters and use no invader tokens (see §19.3; §19.4; §19.15).
rationale: §19.15, added today, is a third campaign that lists named invaders and places no tokens.

old: If a boss's special rules state where the boss is placed or how it faces, those rules replace step 6 (see §17).
new: If a boss's special rules state where the boss is placed or how it faces, those rules replace that part of step 6, and the rest of the step applies (see §17).
rationale: Entries that name only a node (Four Kings, Old Iron King, Asylum Demon, Executioner's Chariot) otherwise lose the starting facing, which the Old Iron King's booklet and back-arc rule require.

old: The boss model is placed on it at the start of every boss encounter (see §15.2).
new: The boss model is placed on it at the start of every boss encounter, unless the boss's special rules name another node (see §15.2; §17).
rationale: Smough, the Asylum Demon and the Old Iron King are placed on other nodes (§17.2, §17.3, §17.10).

old: A boss model is pushed only when another boss model moves onto its node (see §17.1).
new: A boss model is pushed only when another boss model moves onto its node or is placed on it (see §17.1; §17.10, The Four Kings).
rationale: The royal summons places a king on the spawn node and pushes every other model there, a king included (§17.10, step 2).

old: The only push that affects a boss model is the push caused by another boss model moving onto its node (see §17.1).
new: The only push that affects a boss model is the push caused by another boss model that moves onto its node or is placed on it (see §17.1; §17.10, The Four Kings).
rationale: Outside half B; consequential on VB-005, so that §8.4 does not forbid the push that the royal summons requires.

old: In campaign play the spark, the rest, and the setup that follow a boss differ (see §18.1; §18.3).
new: In campaign play the PvP encounter, the spark, the rest, and the setup that follow a boss differ (see §18.1; §18.3).
rationale: Step 6 orders a PvP encounter after every boss; in campaign play it follows only a boss that completes a section (§18.1).

old: When the Pursuer's health is reduced to or below its *heat-up* point {{icon:ast-0030-heat-up-point}}, one random heat-up card is shuffled into its behaviour deck, as for any *boss* (see §15.5). From that moment until the *encounter* ends, the *attack value* of every attack on the Pursuer's behaviour cards is increased by one.
new: When the Pursuer's health is reduced to or below its *heat-up* point {{icon:ast-0030-heat-up-point}}, it heats up as the general rule directs (see §15.5, Heat-Up). From the moment the heat-up is carried out until the *encounter* ends, the *attack value* of every attack on the Pursuer's behaviour cards is increased by one.
rationale: With the heat-up now carried out at the start of the next turn, 'From that moment' had two readings; the wording follows the Old Iron King's entry.

old: The defeat of the Stray Demon does not complete Section Five.
new: The encounters of Section Five are fought in the order listed: the Stray Demon is fought when the first Level 4 encounter is cleared, and the second Level 4 encounter is set up when the Stray Demon is defeated. The defeat of the Stray Demon does not complete Section Five.
rationale: §18.1 sets a mega-boss up after the section's last Level 4 encounter; this section's listed order (and its booklet) puts the Stray Demon between the two.

old: The party may replace the mega-boss of any of these three sections with another mega-boss it owns, and may add further sections of the same form.
new: The party may replace the mega-boss of any of these three sections with another mega-boss it owns, and may add further sections of the same form; the players then win the campaign when every such section is completed.
rationale: 'The players win the campaign when all three are completed' does not hold once further sections are added.

old: When PvP encounters are in play, one *PvP encounter* is fought after each *mini-boss*, *main-boss*, and *mega-boss* is defeated.
new: When PvP encounters are in play, one *PvP encounter* is fought after each *mini-boss*, *main-boss*, and *mega-boss* is defeated. In campaign play it is fought only after a boss whose defeat completes a *section* (see §18.1, Player versus Player Encounters).
rationale: §20.1 owns the rule and lacked the campaign exception made today in §18.1.

old: **A.** Yes, while the characters are on the bonfire tile and at the cost of one *spark*. The new character begins with starting equipment, base stats, and no souls (see §18.4).
new: **A.** Yes, while the characters are on the bonfire tile, no encounter is in progress, and the spark dial shows one or more. The party spends one *spark* for each player who joins. The new character begins with starting equipment, base stats, and no souls (see §18.4).
rationale: The answer omitted two conditions of §18.4: no encounter in progress, and a spark dial that shows one or more.

old: **A.** Yes. The invader vanishes at once and awards nothing, and the encounter continues against the remaining enemy models. The invader does not return (see §12.2, Combat with an Invader).
new: **A.** Yes, unless that death fails the encounter. The invader vanishes at once and awards nothing, and the encounter continues against the remaining enemy models. The invader does not return, unless a campaign states otherwise (see §12.2, Combat with an Invader; §12.2, End of an Invasion).
rationale: The death of a hollow or last character fails the encounter; the rule that the invader does not return, and its campaign exception, stand under End of an Invasion.

old: **A.** Yes. The character is pushed to a valid adjacent node in the arc in which the character is placed. If a wall leaves no such node, the character is pushed to a valid adjacent node that touches the wall (see §15.6, Characters and Arcs).
new: **A.** Yes, except after a *leap*. The character is pushed to a valid adjacent node in the arc in which the character is placed. If a wall leaves no such node, the character is pushed to a valid adjacent node that touches the wall. The push that follows a leap is not limited by arcs (see §15.6, Characters and Arcs; §16.2, Leap).
rationale: The cited section excepts the push that follows a leap.

old: **Round.** One pass of the encounter turn order: every enemy model takes a turn in descending threat order, then every character takes a turn in descending threat order (see §7.5, Encounter Turn Order).
new: **Round.** One pass of the encounter turn order: every enemy model takes a turn in descending threat order, then every character takes a turn in descending threat order (see §7.5, Encounter Turn Order). In a boss encounter a round is one turn by each living character, in an order the players choose, with one boss turn before each of those turns (see §16.1). In a *PvP encounter* a round is one turn by each character still in play (see §20.2).
rationale: The term is used in italics for the rounds of boss encounters (§16.1) and PvP encounters (§20.2, §20.8), which the entry did not cover.

old: after each boss's defeat and before the rest that follows it.
new: after each boss's defeat and before the rest that follows it (in campaign play, only after a boss whose defeat completes a *section*; see §18.1).
rationale: Carries today's campaign rule of §18.1 into the entry.

old: The tier one shop is stocked at setup and the tier two shop when the mini-boss is defeated; both are restocked only after a boss is defeated (in campaign play, after a section is completed), unsold cards going to the bottom of their deck first (see §6.3).
new: The tier one shop is stocked at setup and the tier two shop when the mini-boss is defeated (in campaign play, when the *bonfire ascetic* is burnt); both are restocked only after a boss is defeated (in campaign play, after a section is completed), unsold cards going to the bottom of their deck first (see §6.3; §18.6).
rationale: In campaign play the tier two shop opens with the bonfire ascetic, not with a mini-boss (§18.6, §18.7).

old: **Node.** A circular space on a tile. Every model occupies exactly one node. Nodes are basic, spawn or terrain.
new: **Node.** A circular space on a tile. During an encounter every model occupies exactly one node. Each node is one of three types: basic, spawn, or terrain (see §5.1).
rationale: The entry cited no section; §5.1 states the rule.

old: **Spawn node.** A node on which enemy models are placed at the start of an encounter. Boss tiles have a boss spawn node.
new: **Spawn node.** A node on which enemy models are placed at the start of an encounter, as the encounter card directs. The mini-boss tile, the main-boss tile, and each mega-boss game board have a boss spawn node (see §5.1; §15.3).
rationale: The entry cited no section and omitted the mega-boss spawn node of a game board.

old: **Stamina cube.** A black cube. Each point of stamina a character spends places one stamina cube on the endurance bar, filling from the left.
new: **Stamina cube.** A black cube. Each point of stamina a character spends places one stamina cube on the endurance bar, filling from the left (see §3.4).
rationale: The entry cited no section; §3.4 states the rule.

old: **Transposed treasure.** A class treasure card marked with a blue light. All transposed treasure is tier two.
new: **Transposed treasure.** A *class-specific treasure* card marked with a blue light in the top-right of the card. All transposed treasure is tier two (see §6.2).
rationale: The entry cited no section and named the parent type otherwise than its headword.

old: Encounter rewards and chests draw from tier one until the mini-boss is defeated (in campaign play, until the *bonfire ascetic* is burnt) (see §6.2).
new: Encounter rewards and chests draw from tier one until the mini-boss is defeated (in campaign play, until the *bonfire ascetic* is burnt) (see §6.2; §18.5).
rationale: The campaign clause is stated in §18.5, which was not cited.

old: Encounter rewards and chests draw from tier two once the mini-boss is defeated (in campaign play, once the *bonfire ascetic* is burnt) (see §6.2).
new: Encounter rewards and chests draw from tier two once the mini-boss is defeated (in campaign play, once the *bonfire ascetic* is burnt) (see §6.2; §18.5).
rationale: The campaign clause is stated in §18.5, which was not cited.

old: Each character who died in the boss encounter is revived as after any cleared encounter, except that the ember token of the boss's defeat keeps that character from becoming *hollow*, so no hollow cube is placed (see §7.5, Encounter Recovery; §16.5). The exploration then continues.
new: Each surviving character recovers, and each character who died in the boss encounter is revived, as after any cleared encounter, except that the ember token of the boss's defeat keeps a revived character from becoming *hollow*, so no hollow cube is placed (see §7.5, Encounter Recovery; §16.5). The exploration then continues.
rationale: After a boss that does not complete its section no rest follows, so the survivors recover as after any cleared encounter; otherwise a dead character would return in better state than a living one.
evidence: independent verification, work/phase3/verify_b.md (judgement call decided by the lead editor)

old: Both invaders are part of that encounter every time the characters enter it, until both have been killed during one visit. If either invader vanishes, or the encounter is *failed*, both return the next time the characters enter it.
new: Both invaders are part of that encounter every time the characters enter it, until both have been killed during one visit. If either invader vanishes, or the encounter is *failed*, both return the next time the characters enter it. An encounter that is *cleared* before both of its invaders have been killed is fought again when the characters next enter it, the Level 4 encounter of Section Three included, and it is not skipped.
rationale: Without this the campaign could dead-end: the invaders vanish at a character's death, the survivors clear the encounter, and a cleared Level 4 encounter is otherwise never fought again.
evidence: independent verification, work/phase3/verify_b.md (judgement call decided by the lead editor)
